title: Course Schedule IV
description: Given n courses and direct prerequisite pairs, answer queries asking whether course u is a prerequisite (directly or indirectly) of course v.
hints: n is at most 100, so you can afford to precompute the full "can reach" relation for every pair of courses.
Transitive closure: Floyd-Warshall style reach[i][j] = reach[i][j] or (reach[i][k] and reach[k][j]), or propagate ancestor sets along a topological order.

title: Making A Large Island
description: In an n x n grid of 0s and 1s you may flip at most one 0 to 1. Return the size of the largest island you can end up with.
hints: Label every existing island once and record its size, instead of re-running a flood fill for each 0.
For each 0, add up the sizes of the distinct island ids among its 4 neighbours, plus 1. Remember the grid that is already all 1s.

title: Min Cost to Connect All Points
description: Connect all points on a plane with minimum total Manhattan distance, where any two points can be joined directly.
hints: This is a minimum spanning tree on a complete graph with up to 1000 nodes.
Prim's with a plain O(n^2) array of best distances (no heap, no edge list) beats building all n^2 edges for Kruskal.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
note: redo cold in O(n log n)
description: Return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence of an integer array.
hints: The O(n^2) DP is dp[i] = 1 + max dp[j] over j < i with nums[j] < nums[i]. Now aim lower.
Keep tails[k] = the smallest possible tail of an increasing subsequence of length k+1, and binary search (lower bound) each number into it.

title: House Robber II
description: Houses in a circle hold money and you can't rob two adjacent ones. Maximise the amount robbed.
hints: The circle adds exactly one constraint: the first and last house can't both be taken.
Run linear House Robber twice, on houses [0..n-2] and [1..n-1], and take the max. Handle n = 1 separately.

title: Delete and Earn
description: Taking a value x earns x points but deletes every x-1 and x+1. Maximise your total.
hints: If you take one copy of x you may as well take all of them. Group by value.
Build total[v] = v * count(v); now it's House Robber over the values 0..max.

title: Decode Ways
description: Digits map to letters (1 is A, 26 is Z). Count the ways a digit string can be decoded.
hints: At each position you can consume one digit or two. Zeros are where it goes wrong.
dp[i] = (s[i-1] != '0' ? dp[i-1] : 0) + (two-digit value in 10..26 ? dp[i-2] : 0). Two variables are enough.

title: Word Break
description: Decide whether a string can be split into a sequence of dictionary words.
hints: State: can the prefix of length i be segmented?
dp[i] is true if some j < i has dp[j] true and s[j..i) is in a HashSet. Only look back as far as the longest word.

title: Maximum Product Subarray
description: Find the contiguous subarray with the largest product.
hints: A negative number can turn the smallest product so far into the largest.
Track both the max and the min product ending at i; when nums[i] is negative, swap them before updating.

title: Jump Game II
description: Each value is your maximum jump from that index. Return the minimum number of jumps to reach the last index.
hints: Think in layers: every index reachable with k jumps forms one contiguous range.
Walk i and track the farthest reach; when i reaches the end of the current layer, add a jump and set the layer end to farthest.

title: Unique Paths
description: Count the paths from the top-left to the bottom-right of an m x n grid moving only right or down.
hints: Paths into a cell come only from above or from the left.
One 1D array: dp[j] += dp[j-1], row by row. (Or the closed form C(m+n-2, m-1).)

title: Unique Paths II
description: Same as Unique Paths, but some cells are blocked.
hints: A blocked cell contributes 0 ways, including in the first row and column.
The same 1D DP with dp[j] = 0 on obstacles. Check for an obstacle on the start cell.

title: Minimum Path Sum
description: Find the minimum-sum path from the top-left to the bottom-right moving right or down.
hints: A cell's best cost depends only on the best costs above it and to its left.
dp[i][j] = grid[i][j] + min(up, left), with the first row and column as running sums. Can be done in place.

title: Triangle
description: Find the minimum path sum from the top of a triangle to the bottom, moving to one of the two adjacent numbers on the next row.
hints: Top-down needs care at the edges of each row. Try the other direction.
Bottom-up: dp[j] = row[j] + min(dp[j], dp[j+1]); the answer is dp[0]. O(n) extra space.

title: Minimum Falling Path Sum
description: A falling path takes one element per row of a square matrix, moving straight down or diagonally. Minimise its sum.
hints: Each cell can be reached from at most three cells in the row above.
dp[r][c] = A[r][c] + min of dp[r-1][c-1..c+1] within bounds; the answer is the minimum of the last row.

title: Maximal Square
description: Find the area of the largest square containing only 1s in a binary matrix.
hints: Let the state be the side of the largest all-1 square whose bottom-right corner is (i, j).
dp[i][j] = 1 + min(top, left, top-left) when the cell is '1'. Return the max side squared.

title: Dungeon Game
description: A knight walks right or down through rooms that add or remove health, and health must stay above 0. Find the minimum starting health to reach the bottom-right.
hints: Going forward you'd have to track two things (current health and the lowest it has been). Going backward you only need one.
From the bottom-right: need[i][j] = max(1, min(need[i+1][j], need[i][j+1]) - dungeon[i][j]).

title: Group Anagrams
description: Group strings that are anagrams of each other.
hints: Anagrams share a canonical form. Use it as a map key.
Key = the sorted characters or a 26-count signature; HashMap<String, List<String>>.

title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
description: Find the length of the longest run of consecutive integers in an unsorted array, in O(n).
hints: Sorting is O(n log n). A set lets you ask "is x-1 present?" in O(1).
Only start counting at x when x-1 is not in the set, then walk x+1, x+2 and so on. Each number is touched a constant number of times.

title: Product of Array Except Self
description: For each index return the product of every other element, without division, in O(n).
hints: The answer at i is (product of everything left of i) times (product of everything right of i).
Fill the output with prefix products, then multiply in suffix products on a reverse pass using one running variable.

title: Subarray Sum Equals K
description: Count the contiguous subarrays that sum to k. Values can be negative.
hints: Negatives break sliding windows. Think prefix sums: sum(i..j) = P[j] - P[i-1].
HashMap of prefix sum to how often it was seen, seeded with {0: 1}; at each step add count[P - k].

title: 3Sum
description: Find all unique triplets that sum to zero.
hints: Fix one element; then you need a pair with a known sum in the rest.
Sort; for each i run two pointers on (i+1, n-1). Skip duplicate values for i, and for both pointers after a match.

title: Container With Most Water
description: Pick two vertical lines that, with the x-axis, hold the most water.
hints: The area is limited by the shorter line. Start with the widest container.
Two pointers from both ends; always move the shorter side inward, because moving the taller one can't increase the area.

title: Trapping Rain Water
description: Given bar heights, compute how much rain water is trapped between them.
hints: Water above bar i = min(highest bar to its left, highest to its right) - height[i].
Two pointers: the side with the smaller running max is already decided, so add its water and move it inward. O(1) space.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
description: Find the length of the longest substring whose characters are all distinct.
hints: Grow a window to the right and shrink from the left only when a repeat appears.
Store the last index of each character; on a repeat, left = max(left, last[c] + 1).

title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
description: You may replace up to k characters. Return the length of the longest substring of one repeated letter you can make.
hints: A window is valid when (window length - count of its most frequent letter) <= k.
Keep counts and a maxFreq that never needs to go down; when the window is invalid, slide left by one. The final window size is the answer.

title: Permutation in String
description: Decide whether s2 contains a permutation of s1 as a substring.
hints: The window length is fixed at the length of s1.
Compare 26-count arrays for s1 and the window; slide by adding one character and removing one. A "matches" counter makes each check O(1).

title: Max Consecutive Ones III
description: Find the longest run of 1s if you may flip at most k zeros.
hints: Rephrase: the longest window containing at most k zeros.
Variable window: count zeros and move left while the count exceeds k.

title: Minimum Window Substring
description: Find the smallest substring of s that contains every character of t, counting duplicates.
hints: Grow right until the window covers t, then shrink left as far as it stays valid.
need[] counts plus a "missing" counter; each time missing hits 0, record the window, then shrink.

title: Sliding Window Maximum
description: Return the maximum of every window of size k.
hints: Once a larger element appears after x, x can never be a window maximum again.
A deque of indices with decreasing values: drop expired indices from the front and smaller values from the back.

title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
description: Evaluate an expression in postfix notation with + - * / (division truncates).
hints: Operands wait until their operator arrives.
Stack: push numbers; on an operator pop b, then a, and push a op b. The order matters for - and /.

title: Decode String
description: Expand encoded strings like 3[a2[c]] into accaccacc.
hints: Nesting means you must remember the outer context while you build the inner string.
Two stacks (counts and StringBuilders): on '[' push and reset; on ']' pop and append the current string k times to the popped builder.

title: Daily Temperatures
description: For each day, find how many days you wait until a warmer temperature.
hints: Go left to right and keep the days that are still waiting for a warmer one.
A stack of indices with decreasing temperatures; when a warmer day arrives, pop and set answer[j] = i - j.

title: Car Fleet
description: Cars drive toward a target at fixed speeds and can't overtake; a car that catches up joins that fleet. Count the fleets that arrive.
hints: What matters is when each car would arrive on its own, and the order of positions.
Sort by position descending and compute time = (target - pos) / speed; a new fleet starts whenever a time exceeds the current fleet's time.

title: Remove K Digits
description: Remove k digits from a number string to make it as small as possible.
hints: Removing an earlier digit that is larger than the one after it always helps most.
Increasing stack: pop while the top > current and k > 0; trim from the end if k remains; strip leading zeros; return "0" if empty.

title: Sum of Subarray Minimums
description: Sum min(subarray) over every subarray, modulo 1e9+7.
hints: Flip it: for each element, count how many subarrays it is the minimum of.
Previous-less and next-less-or-equal with monotonic stacks; contribution = arr[i] * left * right. Strict on one side only, to avoid double counting.

title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
description: Find the largest rectangle that fits inside a histogram.
hints: For each bar, the widest rectangle of its height spans to the nearest shorter bar on each side.
Increasing stack of indices; when you pop height h at index i, its width is i - (new top) - 1. A trailing 0 flushes the stack.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
description: Find a target in a rotated sorted array of distinct values in O(log n).
hints: At any mid, at least one half is properly sorted.
Find the sorted half; if the target lies inside its range go there, otherwise go to the other half.

title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
description: Find the minimum of a rotated sorted array of distinct values in O(log n).
hints: Compare mid with the right end, not the left.
If nums[mid] > nums[hi] the minimum is right of mid (lo = mid + 1); otherwise hi = mid.

title: Time Based Key-Value Store
description: Design set(key, value, timestamp) and get(key, timestamp), which returns the value with the largest timestamp not after the given one.
hints: Timestamps for a key arrive in increasing order.
Map each key to a list of (timestamp, value) and binary search for the last timestamp <= the query (or use TreeMap.floorEntry).

title: Koko Eating Bananas
description: Find the minimum eating speed that finishes all piles within h hours, eating from one pile per hour.
hints: If speed s works, every faster speed works too. That monotonic yes/no is the hook.
Binary search s in [1, max pile]; feasible when the sum of ceil(p / s) <= h. Sum in a long.

title: Capacity To Ship Packages Within D Days
description: Find the smallest ship capacity that ships the packages, in order, within d days.
hints: The same shape as Koko: a monotonic yes/no on the capacity.
Search capacity in [max weight, total weight]; greedily fill each day and count the days.

title: Minimum Number of Days to Make m Bouquets
description: Flowers bloom on given days and a bouquet needs k adjacent bloomed flowers. Find the earliest day you can make m bouquets, or -1.
hints: Ask "can I make m bouquets by day D?" and notice the answer only flips once as D grows.
Binary search D; count bouquets by scanning runs of bloomed flowers. Return -1 early if m * k > n (beware overflow).

title: Split Array Largest Sum
description: Split an array into k non-empty contiguous parts so the largest part sum is as small as possible.
hints: Guess the answer instead of constructing the split.
Binary search the cap in [max, sum]; greedily count the parts needed under that cap; feasible if the count <= k.

title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
description: Find the median of two sorted arrays in O(log(m+n)).
hints: Cut both arrays so the left sides together hold half the elements and every left value <= every right value.
Binary search the cut i in the shorter array, j = (m+n+1)/2 - i; check A[i-1] <= B[j] and B[j-1] <= A[i], using infinities at the edges.

title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
description: Remove the n-th node from the end of a linked list in one pass.
hints: Two pointers a fixed distance apart.
Dummy head; move fast n+1 steps, then move both until fast is null; slow.next = slow.next.next.

title: Reorder List
description: Reorder L0, L1, ..., Ln into L0, Ln, L1, Ln-1, ... in place.
hints: It's three classic list operations glued together.
Find the middle (slow/fast), reverse the second half, then merge the two halves alternately.

title: Copy List with Random Pointer
description: Deep-copy a linked list whose nodes also have a random pointer.
hints: You need a way to get from an original node to its copy.
HashMap old to new in two passes; or interleave copies (A, A', B, B'), set randoms, then split the lists for O(1) space.

title: Find the Duplicate Number
description: An array holds n+1 values from 1..n with one value repeated. Find it without changing the array, in O(1) space.
hints: Treat i -> nums[i] as a "next" pointer. What shape does a duplicate create?
Floyd's cycle detection: meet inside the cycle, restart one pointer at 0, and where they meet again is the duplicate.

title: LRU Cache
description: Design a cache with O(1) get and put that evicts the least recently used key.
hints: You need O(1) lookup plus O(1) "move to front" and "remove oldest".
HashMap key to node plus a doubly linked list with dummy head and tail. LinkedHashMap works, but write it yourself for interviews.

title: Reverse Nodes in k-Group
description: Reverse a linked list k nodes at a time; a leftover tail shorter than k stays as it is.
hints: Before reversing a group, check that k nodes exist.
Dummy head; per group find the k-th node, reverse the group in place, connect the previous group's tail to the new head, and move on.

title: Merge k Sorted Lists
description: Merge k sorted linked lists into one sorted list.
hints: At every step you need the smallest head among k lists.
A min-heap of list heads, O(N log k); or merge pairs divide-and-conquer style.

title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
description: Return the node values of a binary tree level by level.
hints: A queue hands back nodes in the order they were discovered.
BFS; each round, read the queue size and pop exactly that many nodes into one level.

title: Binary Tree Right Side View
description: Return the values you'd see looking at a binary tree from the right.
hints: You want exactly one node per depth: the last one at that depth.
BFS taking the last node of each level; or DFS right child first, adding a node when depth == result size.

title: Validate Binary Search Tree
description: Check whether a binary tree is a valid BST with strict ordering.
hints: Comparing a node only with its children isn't enough; each subtree must respect all its ancestors.
Recurse with (low, high) bounds as longs or nullable values; or check that inorder traversal is strictly increasing.

title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
description: Return the k-th smallest value in a BST.
hints: Which traversal visits a BST in sorted order?
Iterative inorder with a stack, stopping at the k-th pop. Keep the counter local, not in a field.

title: Count Good Nodes in Binary Tree
description: A node is good if no node on the path from the root to it has a greater value. Count the good nodes.
hints: Each node only needs to know the largest value on its path from the root.
dfs(node, maxSoFar): count 1 if node.val >= maxSoFar, then recurse with max(maxSoFar, node.val).

title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
description: Rebuild a binary tree with unique values from its preorder and inorder traversals.
hints: Preorder tells you the root; inorder tells you how many nodes go to its left.
HashMap value to inorder index; recurse on index ranges and consume preorder with a pointer. No array copies.

title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
description: Find the lowest common ancestor of two nodes in a binary tree (not a BST).
hints: Ask each subtree: did you find p or q?
Return the node if it is p, q or null; if both sides return non-null this node is the LCA, otherwise pass up the non-null side.

title: Path Sum III
description: Count the downward paths (starting and ending anywhere) whose values sum to a target.
hints: It's Subarray Sum Equals K along every root-to-node path.
DFS with a prefix-sum HashMap: add count[cur - target], increment before recursing and decrement on the way back. Use long.

title: All Nodes Distance K in Binary Tree
description: Return every node exactly k edges away from a target node.
hints: Distances also go upward, and the tree has no parent pointers.
Record parents (or build an adjacency list) with a DFS, then BFS from the target for k levels with a visited set.

title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
description: Find the maximum sum of any path between two nodes of a binary tree.
hints: Separate what you return to your parent (one branch) from what you can complete at this node (both branches).
gain(node) = val + max(0, left, right); update best with val + max(0, left) + max(0, right). Keep best in a holder, not a static field.

title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
description: Design an encoding of a binary tree to a string and back.
hints: One traversal plus explicit null markers is enough to rebuild a tree uniquely.
Preorder with "#" for null, comma-separated; deserialize by recursing over an iterator of tokens.

title: House Robber III
description: Houses form a binary tree and you can't rob a node together with its child. Maximise the loot.
hints: Each node has two states: robbed or not.
DFS returns {rob, skip}: rob = val + left.skip + right.skip; skip = max(left) + max(right).

title: Binary Tree Cameras
description: Place the fewest cameras so every node is watched; a camera covers itself, its parent and its children.
hints: Leaves should never hold cameras; their parents should. Work bottom-up.
Post-order states 0 = not covered, 1 = camera, 2 = covered: a 0 child forces a camera; a camera child means covered; otherwise return 0. Check the root at the end.

title: Top K Frequent Elements
description: Return the k most frequent elements.
hints: Count first; then you need the top k by count.
A min-heap of size k for O(n log k), or bucket sort by frequency for O(n).

title: K Closest Points to Origin
description: Return the k points closest to the origin.
hints: Compare squared distances; no square roots needed.
A max-heap of size k that evicts the farthest, or quickselect for average O(n).

title: Task Scheduler
description: Identical tasks need n idle units between them. Find the minimum total time, idle included.
hints: The most frequent task sets the skeleton of the schedule.
Answer = max(tasks.length, (maxFreq - 1) * (n + 1) + number of tasks that have maxFreq).

title: Single-Threaded CPU
description: A CPU takes tasks by enqueue time; when free it runs the available task with the shortest processing time, ties by index. Return the order.
hints: Two orderings: by arrival to feed tasks in, and by (duration, index) to pick one.
Sort indices by enqueue time; min-heap on (duration, index); if the heap is empty, jump the clock to the next arrival. Time in long.

title: Design Twitter
description: Design post, follow, unfollow and a feed of the 10 most recent tweets from a user and the people they follow.
hints: The feed merges several time-sorted lists, and you only need 10 items.
A global timestamp; per-user tweet lists; a max-heap seeded with each followee's newest tweet (k-way merge).

title: Find Median from Data Stream
description: Support addNum and findMedian on a stream of numbers.
hints: Keep the lower half and the upper half apart.
Max-heap for the lower half, min-heap for the upper, sizes differing by at most 1; rebalance after every add.

title: IPO
description: Starting with capital w, do at most k projects (each needs capital and adds profit) to maximise your final capital.
hints: Among the projects you can currently afford, the most profitable is always the right pick.
Sort by capital; push newly affordable profits into a max-heap; pop the best k times, stopping if the heap is empty.

title: Subsets
description: Return every subset of a set of distinct integers.
hints: Each element is either in or out.
backtrack(start): add a copy of the current list, then for i from start add nums[i], recurse with i+1, remove. Or iterate bitmasks.

title: Combination Sum
description: Find every unique combination of candidates (reuse allowed) that sums to the target.
hints: To avoid duplicate orderings, only move forward through the candidates.
backtrack(start, remain): for i >= start pick candidates[i] and recurse with i, not i+1. Sort to stop early when a candidate > remain.

title: Combination Sum II
description: Same as Combination Sum, but each candidate is used once and the input has duplicates. No duplicate combinations.
hints: Sort so equal values sit together.
Recurse with i+1; at the same depth skip i > start when candidates[i] == candidates[i-1].

title: Permutations
description: Return every permutation of distinct integers.
hints: Each position can take any element not used yet.
Backtrack with a boolean used[] (or swap in place); add a copy when the current list has length n.

title: Word Search
description: Decide whether a word can be traced through adjacent grid cells, using each cell at most once.
hints: DFS from every cell that matches the first letter, marking the path.
Mark the cell (e.g. set it to '#') before recursing and restore it after. Stop early on a mismatch.

title: Palindrome Partitioning
description: Return every way to split a string into palindromic pieces.
hints: Choose the first cut, then solve the rest.
Backtrack over end positions where s[start..end] is a palindrome; precompute isPal[i][j] so you don't recheck.

title: N-Queens
description: Return every placement of n queens on an n x n board where none attack each other.
hints: Exactly one queen per row, so choose a column row by row.
Track used columns and both diagonals (r + c and r - c + n) in boolean arrays for O(1) checks.

title: Jump Game
description: Given maximum jump lengths, decide whether you can reach the last index.
hints: You don't need the path, only how far you can reach.
farthest = max(farthest, i + nums[i]); fail as soon as i > farthest.

title: Gas Station
description: On a circular route with gas and cost at each station, find the start that completes the loop, or -1.
hints: If total gas < total cost it's impossible; otherwise a start exists and it's unique.
Keep a running tank; when it goes negative at i, no start up to i works, so start = i + 1 and reset the tank.

title: Partition Labels
description: Split a string into as many parts as possible so each letter appears in only one part.
hints: A part can't end before the last occurrence of any letter inside it.
Record each letter's last index; extend end = max(end, last[c]); when i == end, close the part.

title: Hand of Straights
description: Decide whether the cards can be split into groups of groupSize consecutive values.
hints: The smallest remaining card has to start a group.
TreeMap of counts; repeatedly take the smallest key x and use up x..x+groupSize-1, failing if any count runs short.

title: Candy
description: Children stand in a line with ratings; each gets at least one candy and a higher-rated child gets more than a neighbour. Minimise the candies.
hints: The left-neighbour rule and the right-neighbour rule can be satisfied separately.
Left pass: c[i] = c[i-1] + 1 when the rating rises. Right pass: c[i] = max(c[i], c[i+1] + 1) when it falls. Sum.

title: Merge Intervals
description: Merge all overlapping intervals.
hints: After sorting by start, an interval can only overlap the last merged one.
Sort by start; if the next start <= last end, extend the end with max; otherwise push a new interval.

title: Insert Interval
description: Insert a new interval into a sorted list of non-overlapping intervals, merging where needed.
hints: Three phases: before, overlapping, after.
Copy intervals that end before the new one starts; merge every interval starting <= the new end into it; copy the rest. O(n), no sort.

title: Non-overlapping Intervals
description: Find the minimum number of intervals to remove so the rest don't overlap.
hints: Flip it: keep as many as possible.
Sort by end; keep an interval if its start >= the last kept end; the answer is n - kept.

title: Divide Intervals Into Minimum Number of Groups
description: Split inclusive intervals into the fewest groups so no two intervals in a group overlap.
hints: The answer equals the largest number of intervals overlapping at one point.
Sort by start; min-heap of group end times; reuse a group if its earliest end < start, else open one. (Or a sweep with +1 and -1 at right+1.)

title: Minimum Interval to Include Each Query
description: For each query, return the size of the smallest interval that contains it, or -1.
hints: Answer the queries offline, in sorted order.
Sort intervals by left and queries by value; push intervals with left <= q into a min-heap on (size, right); pop those with right < q; the top answers q.

title: Coin Change
description: Find the fewest coins (unlimited supply) that make an amount, or -1.
hints: Unbounded knapsack that minimises a count.
dp[a] = min over coins of dp[a - c] + 1, with dp[0] = 0 and amount + 1 as infinity.

title: Coin Change II
description: Count the combinations of coins that make an amount.
hints: Combinations, not permutations: the loop order decides which you count.
Outer loop over coins, inner loop over amounts ascending: dp[a] += dp[a - c], with dp[0] = 1.

title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
description: Decide whether an array can be split into two subsets with equal sums.
hints: Reduce it: is there a subset summing to total / 2?
0/1 knapsack over sums, iterating sums downward for each number (or a BitSet shift). An odd total means false.

title: Target Sum
description: Put + or - before each number and count the ways to reach a target.
hints: Let P be the plus set: sum(P) - (total - sum(P)) = target. Solve for sum(P).
Count subsets with sum (total + target) / 2 using 0/1 knapsack counting; zero ways if that is negative or not whole.

title: Ones and Zeroes
description: Find the largest subset of binary strings using at most m zeros and n ones in total.
hints: A 0/1 knapsack with two capacities.
dp[i][j] = the largest subset with i zeros and j ones; per string, loop i and j downward: dp[i][j] = max(dp[i][j], dp[i-z][j-o] + 1).

title: Last Stone Weight II
description: Smashing stones x <= y leaves y - x. Minimise the weight of the last stone.
hints: The result is the difference between the sums of two groups.
Find the largest reachable subset sum s <= total / 2 (0/1 knapsack); the answer is total - 2s.

title: Book Shop
note: CSES: classic 0/1 knapsack with tight limits
description: Given book prices, page counts and a budget x, maximise the pages you can buy, each book at most once.
hints: Classic 0/1 knapsack with n up to 1000 and x up to 1e5.
A 1D dp over the budget, iterated downward per book. CSES is tight in Java: read input fast (DataInputStream or StreamTokenizer).

title: Longest Common Subsequence
description: Find the length of the longest common subsequence of two strings.
hints: Compare the last characters of the two prefixes.
dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] + 1 if they match, else max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]). Two rows are enough.

title: Edit Distance
description: Find the minimum inserts, deletes and replacements to turn word1 into word2.
hints: The state is a pair of prefixes; each operation shrinks one or both.
dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] if the characters match, else 1 + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1], dp[i-1][j-1]). Base row and column are i and j.

title: Longest Palindromic Substring
description: Return the longest palindromic substring.
hints: Every palindrome has a centre: a character or the gap between two.
Expand around each of the 2n - 1 centres: O(n^2) time, O(1) space. (Manacher is O(n) but rarely expected.)

title: Longest Palindromic Subsequence
description: Find the length of the longest palindromic subsequence.
hints: Interval state: the best answer inside s[i..j].
dp[i][j] = dp[i+1][j-1] + 2 if s[i] == s[j], else max(dp[i+1][j], dp[i][j-1]); fill i from the end. (Or LCS of s and its reverse.)

title: Interleaving String
description: Decide whether s3 is an interleaving of s1 and s2.
hints: After using i characters of s1 and j of s2, the next character of s3 is at i + j.
dp[i][j] = (dp[i-1][j] and s1[i-1] == s3[i+j-1]) or (dp[i][j-1] and s2[j-1] == s3[i+j-1]). Check the lengths first.

title: Distinct Subsequences
description: Count the distinct subsequences of s that equal t.
hints: At s[i], if it matches t[j] you may use it or skip it.
dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + (s[i-1] == t[j-1] ? dp[i-1][j-1] : 0), with dp[i][0] = 1. In 1D, loop j downward.

title: Regular Expression Matching
description: Match a whole string against a pattern with '.' and '*'.
hints: '*' lets the previous element match zero times, or one more time.
dp[i][j] for s[0..i) vs p[0..j): on '*', dp[i][j-2] or (match(s[i-1], p[j-2]) and dp[i-1][j]); otherwise match and dp[i-1][j-1]. Seed dp[0][j] for patterns like a*b*.

title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
description: Implement insert, search and startsWith for a prefix tree.
hints: Each node holds children by letter plus an end-of-word flag.
Node with Node[26] children and a boolean end; walk character by character, creating nodes on insert.

title: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure
description: Like a trie, but search accepts '.' as any letter.
hints: A '.' means trying every child at that level.
Trie plus a recursive dfs(node, index); on '.', loop over the non-null children.

title: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers in an Array
description: Find the maximum XOR of any two numbers in an array.
hints: To maximise XOR, decide bits from the highest down, preferring the opposite bit.
A binary trie over 31 bits; for each number walk the trie preferring the opposite bit to build the best XOR.

title: Word Search II
description: Find every dictionary word that can be traced through adjacent cells of a grid.
hints: Searching for each word separately repeats work. Search for all words at once.
Build a trie of the words; DFS from each cell following trie children; store words at end nodes, clear them once found, and prune empty branches.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Cooldown
description: Maximise stock profit with unlimited transactions but a one-day cooldown after every sale.
hints: Each day you are in one of three states: holding, just sold, or resting.
From yesterday's values: hold = max(hold, rest - p); sold = hold + p; rest = max(rest, sold). The answer is max(sold, rest).

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Transaction Fee
description: Maximise stock profit with unlimited transactions and a fee on each one.
hints: Two states: holding a share or not.
cash = max(cash, hold + p - fee); hold = max(hold, cash - p); start with hold = -prices[0].

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock III
description: Maximise stock profit with at most two transactions.
hints: Four states: after the first buy, first sell, second buy, second sell.
b1 = max(b1, -p); s1 = max(s1, b1 + p); b2 = max(b2, s1 - p); s2 = max(s2, b2 + p). The answer is s2.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock IV
description: Maximise stock profit with at most k transactions.
hints: Generalise the four states of Stock III into arrays of length k.
buy[j] = max(buy[j], sell[j-1] - p); sell[j] = max(sell[j], buy[j] + p). If k >= n/2, it's just unlimited transactions.

title: Minimum Score Triangulation of Polygon
description: Triangulate a convex polygon to minimise the sum, over triangles, of the product of their vertex values.
hints: Edge (i, j) belongs to exactly one triangle, whose third vertex k lies between them.
dp[i][j] = min over i < k < j of dp[i][k] + dp[k][j] + v[i]*v[k]*v[j]; fill by increasing gap.

title: Guess Number Higher or Lower II
description: Each wrong guess x costs x. Find how much money guarantees a win when guessing a number in 1..n.
hints: Minimax: you choose the guess, an adversary chooses the worse side.
dp[l][r] = min over k of k + max(dp[l][k-1], dp[k+1][r]), with dp[l][r] = 0 when l >= r.

title: Minimum Cost to Cut a Stick
description: Cut a stick at given positions in any order; each cut costs the length of the piece being cut. Minimise the total.
hints: Pick which cut happens first inside a segment between two cut points; it splits the problem into two independent segments.
Sort the cuts and add 0 and n; dp[i][j] = min over i < k < j of dp[i][k] + dp[k][j] + (c[j] - c[i]).

title: Burst Balloons
description: Bursting a balloon earns left * it * right using its current neighbours. Maximise the coins.
hints: Choosing the first balloon to burst tangles up the neighbours. Choose the last one instead.
Pad with 1s; dp[l][r] = max over l < k < r of dp[l][k] + dp[k][r] + a[l]*a[k]*a[r], bounds exclusive.

title: Partition to K Equal Sum Subsets
description: Decide whether an array (up to 16 numbers) can be split into k non-empty subsets with equal sums.
hints: With 16 elements, "which ones are used" fits in a bitmask.
dp[mask] = how full the current bucket is (mod target), or -1 if unreachable; add element i when dp[mask] + nums[i] <= target. Sorted backtracking also works.

title: Minimum Number of Work Sessions to Finish the Tasks
description: Fit tasks (up to 14) into the fewest work sessions of at most sessionTime each.
hints: Again a small n: the state is the set of finished tasks.
dp[mask] = (sessions used, time used in the current session), minimised in that order; add one unfinished task at a time, opening a new session when it doesn't fit.

title: Shortest Path Visiting All Nodes
description: Find the shortest walk that visits every node of a small undirected graph (up to 12 nodes); revisits are allowed.
hints: The state is (current node, set of visited nodes).
Multi-source BFS from every (i, 1 << i); the first state with the full mask gives the answer.

title: Elevator Rides
description: People (up to 20) with weights must ride an elevator that holds at most x. Minimise the number of rides.
hints: The same structure as Work Sessions, with tighter limits.
dp[mask] = (rides, weight in the last ride); for each person not in mask, add them to the last ride or start a new one; keep the smaller pair.

title: Range Sum Query - Mutable
description: Support point updates and range sum queries on an array.
hints: Prefix sums make each update O(n). You want both operations in O(log n).
A Fenwick tree (add a delta; query(r) - query(l - 1)) or a segment tree. Try the Fenwick tree, since it's new for you.

title: Count of Smaller Numbers After Self
description: For each element, count the smaller elements to its right.
hints: Go from the right and ask: how many values seen so far are below x?
Compress values to ranks, then a Fenwick tree over ranks: query(rank - 1), then add(rank). Merge-sort counting works too.

title: Dynamic Range Sum Queries
description: Support "set position k to u" and "sum of positions a..b" on an array.
hints: Updates set a value, so turn each into a delta from the current value.
A Fenwick tree with longs, keeping the array to compute deltas. Fast input in Java.

title: Dynamic Range Minimum Queries
description: Support "set position k to u" and "minimum of positions a..b".
hints: Minimum can't be undone like a sum, so prefix tricks don't apply directly.
An iterative segment tree (size 2n, bottom-up update and query) is short and fast.

title: Range Update Queries
description: Support "add u to positions a..b" and "what is the value at position k".
hints: Range update plus point query on the array is point update plus prefix query on its difference array.
Fenwick tree on differences: add(a, u), add(b + 1, -u); the value at k is original[k] + prefix(k).

title: Hotel Queries
description: Hotels in a row have free rooms; each group takes the first hotel with enough rooms. Report the hotel for each group.
hints: You need "the first index whose value >= r", with point updates.
A max segment tree; from the root go left whenever the left child's max >= r; subtract r at the leaf and update upward.

title: Number of 1 Bits
description: Count the set bits of an integer.
hints: n & (n - 1) clears the lowest set bit.
Loop while n != 0 with n &= n - 1, counting. In Java, compare with != 0 rather than > 0 so it works for the sign bit.

title: Counting Bits
description: Return the number of set bits for every number from 0 to n.
hints: Relate i to a smaller number you've already counted.
bits[i] = bits[i >> 1] + (i & 1), or bits[i] = bits[i & (i - 1)] + 1.

title: Single Number II
description: Every element appears three times except one. Find it in O(1) space.
hints: Count each bit position across all numbers, modulo 3.
For each of the 32 bits sum it over all numbers; if the sum % 3 != 0, set that bit in the answer. (Or the ones/twos mask trick.)

title: Sum of Two Integers
description: Add two integers without using + or -.
hints: XOR adds without carries; AND shows where the carries are.
Loop: carry = (a & b) << 1; a = a ^ b; b = carry; until b == 0. Java's two's complement handles negatives.

title: Pow(x, n)
description: Compute x raised to the power n.
hints: x^n = (x^(n/2))^2, times x when n is odd.
Fast exponentiation with long N = n (negating Integer.MIN_VALUE overflows); if N < 0, invert x first.

title: Multiply Strings
description: Multiply two non-negative numbers given as strings.
hints: Digit i of one number times digit j of the other lands in positions i + j and i + j + 1.
An int[m + n] result; add products from the right, carry forward, then build the string without leading zeros.

title: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1)
description: Design a set with average O(1) insert, remove and getRandom.
hints: Random picks need an array; O(1) removal from an array needs a trick.
ArrayList plus HashMap value to index; to remove, move the last element into the gap and update its index.

title: Design Underground System
description: Track check-ins and check-outs and report the average travel time between two stations.
hints: Two maps: trips in progress, and stats for finished routes.
id to (station, time); "from,to" to (total time, count), updated on check-out.

title: LFU Cache
description: Design a cache that evicts the least frequently used key, ties broken by least recent use, all in O(1).
hints: Group keys by frequency, and keep recency order inside each group.
key to node, frequency to LinkedHashSet (or a DLL) of keys, plus minFreq; on access move the key to freq + 1; on insert minFreq = 1.

title: Rotting Oranges
description: Each minute, fresh oranges next to rotten ones rot. Return the minutes until none are fresh, or -1.
hints: Every rotten orange spreads at the same time. What processes things in waves?
Multi-source BFS from all rotten cells, counting levels; then check that no fresh orange is left.

title: Longest Continuous Subarray With Absolute Diff Less Than or Equal to Limit
description: Find the longest subarray whose max - min is at most limit.
hints: If a range is valid, every range inside it is too. What does that let two indices do?
A sliding window with two monotonic deques (for max and min); shrink while max - min > limit.

title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
description: Water flows to neighbours of equal or lower height. Find the cells that can reach both the top/left ocean and the bottom/right ocean.
hints: Asking "where can this cell flow?" for every cell repeats work. Turn the question around.
Search uphill (to heights >= current) from each ocean's border cells; the answer is the cells reached by both.

title: Meeting Rooms III
description: Meetings take the lowest-numbered free room, or wait for the room that frees first and keep their length. Which room hosts the most meetings?
hints: Simulate in start order. Each meeting needs both "lowest free room" and "busy room that finishes first".
Two heaps: free rooms by number, busy rooms by (end, number). Free every room ending <= start; if none are free, delay to the earliest end. Use long times.

title: Number of Ways to Arrive at Destination
description: Count the shortest paths from 0 to n-1 in a weighted graph, modulo 1e9+7.
hints: You need the shortest distance and, alongside it, how many ways reach it.
Dijkstra with long distances; on a strictly shorter distance set ways[v] = ways[u]; on an equal one add ways[u].

title: Subarrays with K Different Integers
description: Count the subarrays with exactly k distinct values.
hints: "Exactly k" is awkward to count directly. "At most k" is easy.
exactly(k) = atMost(k) - atMost(k - 1), each a sliding window with a count map.

title: Word Ladder
description: Find the length of the shortest chain from beginWord to endWord, changing one letter at a time through dictionary words.
hints: Each word is a node; a one-letter change is an edge, and every edge costs the same.
BFS; generate neighbours by trying 26 letters per position against a HashSet (remove when visited), or use wildcard patterns like h*t.

title: Jump Game VI
description: Jump 1 to k steps forward each time; your score is the sum of values you land on. Maximise the score at the end.
hints: dp[i] = nums[i] + the best dp in the last k positions. Done naively that's O(nk).
Keep the window max with a deque of indices whose dp values decrease.

title: Swim in Rising Water
description: At time t you can swim through cells with elevation <= t. Find the earliest time you can reach the bottom-right.
hints: A path's cost is its highest cell, not its sum.
A min-heap on max-so-far (Dijkstra style), or binary search t with BFS, or union-find adding cells by height.

title: Maximal Rectangle
description: Find the largest rectangle of 1s in a binary matrix.
hints: Fix the bottom row of the rectangle and look at the columns of 1s standing on it.
Build column heights row by row and run Largest Rectangle in Histogram (monotonic stack) on each row.

title: Find All People With Secret
description: Person 0 tells firstPerson a secret at time 0, and meetings at the same time pass it on instantly. Return everyone who ends up knowing it.
hints: Meetings at the same moment form groups, but links must not carry over to later times.
Sort by time; per time batch, union the pairs, then reset every person in the batch who isn't connected to 0. (Or BFS per batch.)

title: Minimum Number of Operations to Make Array Continuous
description: An array is continuous when its values are unique and max - min = n - 1. One operation replaces any element. Minimise operations.
hints: Choose which values to keep; they must fit in a range of length n.
Sort the unique values; for each start v count uniques in [v, v + n - 1] with two pointers; the answer is n - most kept.

title: Shortest Path in a Grid with Obstacles Elimination
description: Find the shortest path from top-left to bottom-right if you may remove up to k obstacles.
hints: The position alone isn't enough state.
BFS over (r, c, removals left) with visited per state. Shortcut: if k >= m + n - 2 the answer is m + n - 2.

title: Shortest Subarray with Sum at Least K
description: Find the shortest non-empty subarray with sum at least k; values can be negative.
hints: Negatives break a plain sliding window. Think in terms of P[j] - P[i] >= k.
A deque of prefix indices with increasing sums: pop the front while P[j] - P[front] >= k (record the length); pop the back while P[back] >= P[j]. Use long.

title: Minimum Cost to Make at Least One Valid Path in a Grid
description: Each cell has an arrow, and changing one costs 1. Find the minimum cost to make a path from the top-left to the bottom-right.
hints: Following the arrow costs 0; any other move costs 1.
0-1 BFS with a deque: 0-cost moves to the front, 1-cost moves to the back (or Dijkstra).

title: Reconstruct Itinerary
description: Use every airline ticket exactly once to build the lexicographically smallest itinerary starting at JFK.
hints: Using every edge exactly once is a well-known problem with a name.
Hierholzer's algorithm: adjacency lists as min-heaps; DFS consuming edges, add each airport post-order, then reverse.

title: Largest Color Value in a Directed Graph
description: A path's color value is how often its most common color appears. Return the largest over all paths, or -1 if the graph has a cycle.
hints: Handle cycles first; on a DAG you can push information along edges in order.
Kahn's topological sort with dp[node][26] = the best count of each color on paths ending at node; if not every node is processed, return -1.
